rateLimits.note: Nominatim's usage policy: "an absolute maximum of 1 request per second", the traffic of all the application's users together. A script running longer than a day or at regular intervals (bulk geocoding) is held to 4 requests a minute, one thread, one machine: a site declares that limit itself (policy) when it geocodes in bulk. GeocoderPhp keeps one call a second per process (nominatim_interval) and caches answers (geocoder_ttl).

provenance.notes: The OpenStreetMap Foundation's servers (tile.openstreetmap.org, nominatim.openstreetmap.org): what this policy declares; another tile server or Nominatim instance has its own terms, which the site adds (policy). Tiles: a distinct, stable User-Agent naming the application (no library default, no browser imitation), a Referer from browsers, the attribution visible on the map ("© OpenStreetMap contributors", usually bottom right, never hidden); Cache-Control, Expires and ETag honoured, at least 7 days when they cannot be read, conditional requests for expired tiles; no bulk download, prefetching or pre-seeding, no offline use ("download for offline", "save area for later"), no wide-area scans (z>=14). The tile policy sets no request rate nor concurrency: none declared. Nominatim: a User-Agent or Referer identifying the application, results cached, no autocomplete, no systematic queries (a grid of reverse queries, every postcode), no reselling of results; the service must be switchable off without a software update. Both: best effort, access may be blocked without notice, no separate commercial terms (commercial services may lose access at any point). Storage and redistribution left unknown: the data is ODbL (share-alike), the tiles may not be kept for offline use.
